citation.note: Written Notice at Hire: Montana has no required written notice to the employee at hire about at-will status or wage-theft prevention; no state form mandated.

citation.note: Payroll records and remuneration documents retained at least 4 years after the calendar year paid (stricter than the 3-year federal FLSA rule); no paper-vs-electronic mandate.

No frequency mandate (weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly all allowed); wages may not be held more than 10 business days after earned and due; written notice of wage rate and pay date before hire (MCA § 39-3-204).

Final pay timing: MCA § 39-3-205 requires immediate payment on involuntary termination unless the employer has a written policy extending to the next payday or 15 days, whichever is sooner. Resignations: next regular payday or 15 days, whichever sooner.

body.deadline_description: Immediate payment on involuntary termination unless a written policy extends to the next payday or 15 days, whichever sooner; resignations due next regular payday or 15 days (MCA § 39-3-205).

citation.note: Employment non-competes generally void; enforceable only for sale of goodwill or partnership dissolution, plus narrow judicial exceptions; flag any employment covenant for legal review.

body.rule: Employment non-competes generally void; enforceable only for sale of goodwill or partnership dissolution, plus narrow judicial exceptions; flag any employment covenant for legal review.

citation.note: Minimum wage ties to CPI-U annually: MCA § 39-3-404; as of 2026-01-01, $10.85/hour (adjusted annually by inflation, rounded to nearest $0.05).

citation.section: (statutory section not stated in the research file)
citation.note: Deductions and Pay Statements: Montana follows federal FLSA rules; only deductions required by law, court order, or written employee authorization are permitted.
Discrimination and Protected Classes (MCA § 49-2-303): Ensure pay changes and terminations do not violate discrimination statutes.

WDEA good-cause standard after probation: default 12-month probation, extendable once by up to 6 months (18 total); post-probation discharge requires good cause; internal-grievance exhaustion with a 90-day safety valve.

Breach of computerized personal information requires notice to affected residents without unreasonable delay (3-5 business days recommended) (MCA § 30-14-1704).
